summary.headline: The Tricentennial Committee reviewed planning for the 2027 celebration, including a music festival, drone show, and street banner installations.
summary.summary: The Southborough Tricentennial Committee received updates on major event planning for the town's upcoming 300th anniversary celebration in 2027. Organizers presented progress on the August 2027 music festival and a New Year's drone show, alongside a proposed winter bonfire and village street banners. The committee also discussed town history projects, parade participation, daffodil planting with the Garden Club, and potential state budget earmarks.

topics.title: Music festival update
topics.summary: The working group lead presented initial plans for the Southborough Tricentennial Spectacular music festival, targeted for August 21, 2027, at the Neary school complex. The proposed eight-hour event would run from 1:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., integrating elements of the recreation department's Summer Nights program with up to six musical acts and fireworks. The working group is reviewing stage rental costs estimated between $15,000 and $17,000, potential performers, and the viability of a beer garden.
key_details: Event date targeted for Saturday, August 21, 2027, from 1:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. at the Neary complex.
Expected attendance estimated at 4,000 to 5,000 people.
Current budget placeholder stands between $15,000 and $25,000, with stage and audio rentals estimated at $15,000 to $17,000.
Organizers are distributing a performer talent survey and exploring headliners as well as local bands.
A proposal for an enclosed beer garden will require consultation with the school department and Select Board regarding alcohol policies on town property.
topics.outcome: The working group will refine the event program, firm up stage quotes, and report back at a future meeting.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the meeting minutes from its April 8, 2026, meeting with minor typographical corrections.
key_details: Meeting minutes of April 8, 2026, approved as amended.

topics.title: AI-generated town history presentation
topics.summary: A committee member presented a demonstration of a 20-chapter town history project generated with artificial intelligence audio software. The chapters cover Southborough history milestones including Native American history, the 1740 distemper epidemic, the Burnett and Fay families, and historic mills. The committee discussed reviewing the audio samples and exploring whether the material could be used online, in schools, or as part of tricentennial media.
key_details: Project features 20 short chapters covering major events in Southborough history set to musical accompaniment.
Material is royalty-free and can be edited, shortened, or adapted for visual displays.
A sample link will be sent to committee members to review before the June meeting.
topics.outcome: The committee will review the audio materials for discussion at its June meeting.

topics.title: First Night and First Day drone show planning
topics.summary: The recreation director outlined plans for the First Night and First Day kickoff celebration scheduled for January 1, 2027. The proposed schedule features daytime wellness activities and yoga at the Senior Center, children's and family activities at Woodward School, food trucks, and an evening drone light show at St. Mark's field around 6:00 p.m. Organizers are working on cost estimates for custodial coverage, police details, and ice sculptures.
key_details: Event scheduled for Friday, January 1, 2027.
Proposed locations include the Senior Center, Woodward School, and St. Mark's field for the evening drone show.
The drone light show is estimated at approximately $25,000 within a total $30,000 day budget.
Organizers will seek to include adult and senior-oriented afternoon programming in addition to children's activities.
topics.outcome: The recreation director will prepare a detailed budget and schedule for future review.

topics.title: Town bonfire proposal
topics.summary: The committee discussed options for hosting a large community bonfire as part of the anniversary year. Members debated whether to hold it in mid-January following Christmas tree collection or move it to the fall of 2026 or 2027 to avoid harsh weather and conflicts with the January 1 kickoff. Two potential locations are under consideration: the Neary school grounds and Finn school.
key_details: Possible locations under consideration are the Neary complex and Finn school.
Members discussed using wood pallets rather than Christmas trees, which allows more seasonal flexibility.
Coordination is required with the Fire Department, Conservation Commission, and School Department before setting a date.
topics.outcome: Topic tabled for further coordination with town boards and public safety officials.

topics.title: Utility pole banners and village displays
topics.summary: Members reviewed a detailed Department of Public Works map showing town utility poles that have street lighting hardware. The committee is planning banner placements across Southborough's four historic villages, Main Street, and school zones. Discussions centered on banner dimensions, mounting hardware, clearances, and budget limits.
key_details: Considering banner dimensions of 24 by 36 inches or 18 by 24 inches in 18-ounce outdoor vinyl.
Town bylaw allows commemorative banners to be installed starting in August 2026 through the end of 2027.
Targeting a minimum of four banners per village center plus key road corridors.
DPW and utility companies must confirm allowable mounting heights and safety clearances.
topics.outcome: Members will investigate installation clearance limits and develop formal cost estimates.

topics.title: Garden Club and town plantings
topics.summary: The Southborough Gardeners confirmed dates for the 'History in Bloom' floral and art exhibition, to take place April 15–17, 2027, at the Southborough Library. The club also confirmed its participation in the tricentennial parade and proposed a large-scale daffodil planting in fall 2026 that would bloom in spring 2027. The committee debated planting a large numeral '300' display on a prominent town hillside.
key_details: History in Bloom event confirmed for April 15–17, 2027, at the Southborough Library.
Garden Club confirmed it will enter a decorated truck and walking unit in the parade.
Proposed daffodil planting in fall 2026 for spring 2027 bloom, requiring town equipment to clear ground.
Wholesale daffodil bulbs estimated at roughly 50 to 65 cents per bulb.
topics.outcome: The committee will follow up with DPW on machinery support for site preparation.

topics.title: General event and committee updates
topics.summary: The committee conducted rapid updates on several ongoing initiatives, including Family Day at Fay School, social media awareness posts, the oral history project, and parade contract templates. Members also discussed anniversary merchandise, including holiday ornaments, and noted that communication is underway with State Representative Kate Donahue regarding a potential $20,000 to $30,000 state budget earmark for the celebration.
key_details: Oral history project has received strong resident interest through local social media groups.
Town counsel reviewed standard parade contract forms, which will be finalized shortly.
Tricentennial commemorative holiday ornaments and merchandise items are under review with the fundraising group.
State Representative Kate Donahue's office has been contacted regarding a potential state budget earmark in the $20,000 to $30,000 range.
topics.outcome: Information accepted; committee representatives will deliver an update to the Select Board on June 16, 2026.
